messages:
maria: quick q — we found a tokenizer default that was producing slightly different tokenization for emojis. fix is trivial, but it changes output for some edge prompts. do we treat this as a patch or a minor? planning a hotfix today.
kevin: if it's only a bugfix with no API surface change it's usually a patch (x.y.z). semantics-only doc says patch for bugfix
anya: hmm it changes default behavior/output though. some customers may see diffs. i'd argue minor if outputs can change even with same API
samir: what's our policy for 'behavioral changes'? i thought minor was reserved for added/backwards-compatible features, not default tweaks
leo: support report: two customers may be impacted, both internal testbeds, not prod-critical. they'd prefer opt-in but this is a correctness fix
maria: right — this is a correctness/security-ish change (tokenization correctness). want to be consistent: do we treat output-affecting correctness as patch or minor?
kevin: pragmatic take: patch if it's a bugfix that restores intended behavior. minor if it intentionally changes the default experience. this IS restoring intended behavior -> patch.
anya: i worry about downstream reproductions. if we ship a patch that changes outputs people will be confused. we should be explicit in release notes and maybe roll it out slowly
samir: proposal: branch strategy: create `hotfix/v1.4.3` -> tag `v1.4.3`. open backport PRs to release-1.3. keep tag clean (no '-hotfix' suffix) so semver tooling works
leo: agree with keeping tags clean. for visibility add a changelog line: "tokenizer: restore intended emoji splitting (may change outputs)" and mark as IMPORTANT in notes
anya: also we should update our semver docs: add a clause "changes to defaults or output semantics count as minor unless they fix correctness that was a regression" — but that's vague
kevin: concrete suggestion for doc: "patch: fixes that restore documented behavior or correct regressions without adding features. minor: changes that alter documented defaults or introduce new non-bug behavior." simple and actionable
maria: ok plan then: classify this as patch (since it's a regression/correctness). will do branch `hotfix/v1.4.3`, tag `v1.4.3`, create release note emphasizing changed outputs, schedule rollout outside EU business hours. also open backport PR to 1.3.
deploy-bot: deploy queued by @maria — target=production, branch=hotfix/v1.4.3, eta=30m, changelog="tokenizer: restore intended emoji splitting"
kevin: i'll add a regression prompt set and CI check. here's the tag command i'll run: `git tag -a v1.4.3 -m "hotfix(tokenizer): restore emoji tokenization"`
samir: i'll review the hotfix PR now and approve. also will watch logs during rollout
anya: thanks — i still want the semver doc edit as follow-up issue. can someone open a small RFC to lock down wording? keeps future debates shorter
maria: will open RFC and a docs PR right after deploy. rolling at 22:30 UTC. @samir please merge after green CI and my approval
samir: :thumbsup: merging after checks
maria: thanks everyone, i'll paste the release note snippet here once created"
